claims.text: Post-deposition thermal annealing will enhance the magnetocaloric effect of non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type nanoscale films or nanoribbons.
Post-deposition thermal annealing will reduce magnetic hysteresis in non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type nanoscale films or nanoribbons.
Annealing reduces structural disorder in the deposited alloy.
Annealing relieves residual stresses in the deposited alloy.
Annealing reduces nanoscale defects and defect-induced magnetic pinning sites.
Reduced disorder, residual stress, and pinning improve magnetic-domain alignment.
Annealing promotes a more coherent and reversible magnetic-domain configuration.
A more coherent and reversible magnetic-domain configuration increases the magnetocaloric response.
A more coherent and reversible magnetic-domain configuration decreases magnetic hysteresis.
Annealed samples will exhibit a larger magnetocaloric temperature change than the as-deposited baseline.
Annealed samples will exhibit a smaller magnetic-hysteresis-loop area than the as-deposited baseline.
As-deposited thin films or nanoribbons typically have a lower magnetocaloric response than annealed samples.
As-deposited thin films or nanoribbons typically have higher magnetic hysteresis than annealed samples.
The proposed effect applies during magnetic-cooling cycles at applied fields below 1 T near the operative magnetic transition temperature.
Heat-transfer limitations constrain the usable magnetic-cooling cycle frequency.
The annealing effect may depend on film thickness, annealing temperature, and annealing duration.
